solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sorry revolutionary alien stops in Jerusalem arms proposal

indicators.note: in says the whole assembly is placed within the name for Jerusalem

parts.note: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and a poetic name for the city

indicators.note: the reversed word stops up, or plugs, the alien's two letters

parts.note: ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sorry in the sense of pitiful or wretched, poor

explanation.surface: A regretful extraterrestrial halts a weapons negotiation in the Holy City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the word for sorry round; 'stops' plugs that into the film alien, and 'in' sets the lot inside the biblical name for Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: The zero option was a Cold War disarmament offer to remove all intermediate missiles, a proposal about weapons.

clue.text: From the South Temperate Zone, letter enclosed

indicators.note: From the South says the hidden letters are read backwards
enclosed says the letters sit inside the phrase Temperate Zone

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A geography note: a letter sent from the southern temperate belt with something enclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'letter enclosed' as the definition, but 'enclosed' is the signal that the letters are held within 'Temperate Zone'; the definition is just 'letter'. In a down clue, 'From the South' means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeta is the sixth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter.

clue.text: Ham actors in film plastered and stoned?

parts.note: ham acting is crude or rough
the actors in a film are its cast

explanation.surface: Overacting film players turn up drunk and high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered and stoned' reads as drunk and drugged, but it is literal: the coating is plaster mixed with small stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast is a wall rendering of plaster with gravel or pebbles in it, so a wall so treated is plastered and stoned.

clue.text: The retrospective father of history angry about bigger priorities

indicators.note: about says the shuffled letters go around the other pieces
angry means agitated, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A cross reviewer of Herodotus, the so-called father of history, has more important things to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The father of history' points at Herodotus, a dead end. 'angry' shuffles OF HISTORY, which goes 'about' THE and RF ('retrospective' turning FR).
explanation.definitionFit: To have other matters to attend to is an idiom for having more important things to deal with.

clue.text: Ultimately, Cousteau implicating sub in bang on water tower

indicators.note: in says those letters go inside the phrase for bang on

parts.note: bang on means exactly right, to a T

indicators.note: Ultimately picks the final letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Jacques Cousteau's submarine blows up on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water tower' is not a building: it is a vessel that tows on water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a small powerful vessel that pulls ships, so it is something that tows on water.

clue.text: Reduced variable? I'm not sure

parts.note: a switch that is on-off can vary between two states
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating over whether a quantity was cut or merely changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are reduced in price are available at a special price in a sale.

clue.text: Status Quo stealing lead from another rock band

indicators.note: taking away the lead means removing the first letter

parts.note: Oasis is a British rock band, like Status Quo

explanation.surface: The rock group Status Quo poaches a lead singer from a rival band.
explanation.walkthrough: Status Quo looks like the band, but the definition is the Latin phrase for the existing state.
explanation.definitionFit: The status quo is things left unchanged, in their present condition.

clue.text: Needles and pins finally secure position, some say

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of pins
some say means the words are spoken, so their sound gives the letters

parts.note: secure is tie and position is lie; said together, tie-lie

explanation.surface: Sewing advice: needles and pins hold things in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Styli are the pointed tips that run in a record's groove, gramophone needles.

clue.text: Steady hum personalised by music-maker

parts.note: a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, a squeeze
a hum is a smell, and a personal one is body odour, BO
by as in multiplication, three by four, is written x

explanation.surface: A constant drone made personal by an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezebox is a familiar name for the accordion or concertina, an instrument.

clue.text: Approximate location of 13 in the air

parts.note: round means approximate, as in a round figure
13 down is the nursery-rhyme boy who sat in a corner

explanation.surface: Roughly where the nursery-rhyme boy is to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approximate location' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits after 'Approximate'; the boy of 13 sat in a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the air is imminent, about to happen, just as a thing near at hand is.

clue.text: A little too much, but not over 1000

indicators.note: but not says some letters are taken away from the phrase before it

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A small amount too many, though not more than a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking O and M from TOO MUCH leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch is a small amount, as in a touch of salt.

clue.text: Young cooks dressing ducks to render well done at barbie?

indicators.note: dressing means covering, so the rearranged letters wrap the rest
cooks means the letters are worked over into a new form

parts.note: a duck is zero in cricket, the letter O, so two ducks are OO
to render a song is to do it

explanation.surface: Young chefs dressing duck so that it comes out well done on the barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well done' looks like cooking but is praise; 'barbie' is Australian for barbecue, hinting at Australian speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian phrase is a hearty congratulation, the same as saying bravo.

clue.text: Thing I like about much of East Anglia I have summarised, bringing flattery to an end?

parts.note: a charm is something attractive, a thing one likes
about in the sense of concerning, as in tales of
the Fens are low wetlands covering much of East Anglia
I have, shortened, is I've

explanation.surface: A traveller praises the fenlands of eastern England while cutting short the compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: THE FENS are flat drained marshland in eastern England. 'bringing' is a link; the definition is flattery used for a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign of flattery and friendliness aimed at winning support is flattery used as a means to an end.

clue.text: Fellow congratulating himself on plum job's giving troublesome anchor jerk

definitions.text: Fellow congratulating himself on plum job

indicators.note: something troublesome is unruly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man pleased with his cushy post has trouble with a jerking anchor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plum job' looks like a cushy post, but the nursery-rhyme boy pulled a plum from a pie and said 'what a good boy am I'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the boy pulls a plum from his pie and praises himself.

clue.text: Asian scholar rating one son in school subject

indicators.note: in says the middle pieces go inside the subject

parts.note: art is a subject taught in school
an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A scholar of Asia grades one boy in an academic subject.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in the language and culture of the Arab world, which lies largely in western Asia.

clue.text: Cat not getting at cream runs back round attached network

indicators.note: round says the reversed letters go around the remnant of Cat
back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the cream of a group is its elite
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: not getting means the letters at are removed from Cat

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat denied its cream runs back to a linked network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ELITER into RETILE; Cat without AT leaves C, which goes inside. 'attached' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticle is a grid of fine crossed lines in the eyepiece of a telescope or sight.

clue.text: Won a tidy sum?

definitions.meaning: made a big profit, scooped the pool
read literally, a sum that has been tidied, made neat

explanation.walkthrough: 'tidy sum' means a large amount, but taken literally a tidy sum is one that has been made neat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both made a large profit and made clean and neat.

clue.text: What comes from vessel with increased vigour!

definitions.text: What comes from vessel with increased vigour!

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel
something increased has gone up

explanation.surface: Sauce reluctantly emerging from its bottle only after harder shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes tomato sauce coming out of the bottle once it is shaken harder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato sauce famously refuses to leave the bottle until it is thumped or shaken vigorously.

clue.text: Parking, the one everyone's chasing will power nap on journey?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
in the game of tag the chaser is it; the one everyone chases will be it, put as it is to, since is to can mean will
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Will Power, the IndyCar driver everyone chases, grabs a quick rest on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will power' tempts as determination, or as the racing driver Will Power; 'will' ends the phrase it is to, and 'power' gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief halt for rest or refreshment on a long road trip is a break, like a short sleep.

clue.text: Round these parts, very strong winds as well

indicators.note: Round says the turned letters go around the place word
winds means turns back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive or very strong
round these parts means here

explanation.surface: A weather report: in this area there are gales too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like weather but signals turning back; the turned letters split around the place word.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal adverb means in addition to that, besides.

clue.text: You and I, out of wet suit, collected culture

indicators.note: out of says the pair is taken away from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
you and I together are we
hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Two divers leave their wetsuits and gather some culture.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing WE from WET leaves T; 'collected' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, music, literature and theatre together make up culture.

clue.text: Off in pursuit of Dracula?

definitions.meaning: unconscious, knocked out, as a boxer floored for ten seconds
Dracula is a Count, so chasing him is going after that nobleman

explanation.walkthrough: A boxer floored for the referee's count of ten is out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means knocked out cold or fast asleep, unconscious.

clue.text: Every so often, at this organ?

definitions.meaning: occasionally is put as at the word in question, at intervals
an organ is a newspaper, here the London daily

explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks anatomical or musical, but it means a newspaper, the London daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Put after at it means occasionally, and the name is that of a famous British newspaper.

clue.text: Used to be the Telegraph crossword compilers? Touching!

parts.note: setters refer to themselves as we, and this clue appeared in the Telegraph
touching means concerning, re

explanation.surface: Were the Telegraph's setters ever moving? How touching!
explanation.definitionFit: The past plural of the verb to be describes what formerly existed.

clue.text: In return race, nursing injured toe and arm, one's over the line!

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so the reversed word cradles the rest
return means the word is turned back

parts.note: a run is a race

indicators.note: injured means damaged or bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner with a hurt toe and arm crosses the finish line in a return race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' gives MERATO. 'over the line' looks like a finish but means above a fraction bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction the top number sits above the dividing line.

clue.text: Prompt, in altogether grand opening

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: in the altogether means naked

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of grand

explanation.surface: A prompt arrival, all together, for a grand opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone is to give them a gentle push or poke.

clue.text: File using this could make for fop

parts.note: turning the word for into fop means writing its R as a P

explanation.surface: Using a file could turn a word into a dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as R AS P, the answer is an instruction: write R as P, and 'for' becomes 'fop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse metal tool with raised teeth, used for shaping wood, is a kind of file.

clue.text: In a mobile shop, knocking back wine's close to the mark

indicators.note: In says the reversed drink goes into the other letters
mobile means moving, so the letters are rearranged
knocking back means drinking, and here also turning the word round

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: close to picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone downing wine in a mobile shop is near the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' gives POSH; 'knocking back' makes TROP; 'wine's' only seems to hold the closing letter, which comes from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol showing possession or omission is a mark.
